At the conference in Vienna in September 1998, Jon Keating delivered a lecture during

sophisticated geometrical space called the noncommutative space of adele classes. His

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Random-walk behavior explains plausible average cancellation, yet sharp pointwise bounds can fail at enormous scales and a probability model may still tolerate off-critical-line zeros.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The weaker epsilon-relaxed Mertens condition remains equivalent to RH; failure of the stronger heuristic does not refute RH.
